comment: I took this class for a credit requirement and would have dropped immediately if I had the option to do so. The course itself isn't that difficult, just EXTREMELY boring. You can easily get away with not participating/not doing the assigned reading, but Davis is an incredibly harsh grader and your grade is soley dependent on three papers.

Professor Davis gives some pretty great lectures, but he is an incredibly hard grader. I took him for my first year seminar, and he basically expected us to write professional level papers. His class definitely helped my writing style as a whole, but he only grades off of 3 papers for the entire semester. His Tolkien class is extremely informative.

Conflicted feelings about Professor Davis. He's a great guy, pretty funny, and does his best in making the reading topics interesting. However, the entire class grade hinges on three ten-page papers with uninteresting and unclear prompts. Don't expect to get an A unless you make your FYS your number 1 priority. He does give okay feedback on papers.

There are two papers which make up the entire grade, but Davis is one of the funniest and most engaging professors I've ever had. You can tell when he talks that he knows a ton about his subject. He's also very easy to get off track, but his stories are totally worth it

Davis is hilarious, but its also clear he cares about his students. Hes an extremely smart guy and he helped me become a much stronger writer. He also tries extremely hard to make class engaging and interesting. 10/10 personality too.

I loved this class so much! So so interesting. Davis's papers are hard but if you go to him for help he will read your whole essay. Be prepared when you come to class or else its obvious. Will definitely take another class with him, the discussions will change your mindset on a lot of things. The readings were great. Difficult but worth it.

Cool enough guy who engages his students by talking about weird subjects that'll make you laugh but think at the same time. Kind of a difficult grader, but the class is pretty easy as a whole as I haven't read any of his books all year and am doing just fine.

Dr. Davis has a sharp whit and is very intellectual. He has taught at Princeton and I believe other top institutions in the past. He does not disparage his students or talk down on their intelligence. However, make sure you understand his questions and make an effort to answer them. 3 papers make up your entire grade, so take your time with those

Dr. Davis is a great professor. There is a lot of reading but as long as you get the gist if it and can talk about it, you're fine. Papers are challenging but Dr. Davis is a great help if you're willing to put in the work.
He's fun in class, and clearly very intelligent.
davis is awesome. a little challenging but very funny professor. not too much work. lots of weird/hilarious anecdotes about his crazy life experiences. great option for an otherwise dreadful class.

Dr. Davis is amazingly intellectual... Now that may scare you as it did me but pretty much after the first week you figure out whats going on.... After that good guy goes off on random topics which is always good and only has 5 papers compared to a paper every class... Good guy not great class but considering the other options amazing
Good teacher. Take him if you wanna learn how to write well. He'll make sure you learn. Or you'll flunk his class. Either or.

i loved prof. davis...he is incredibly smart and really funny...this was my first class with him, and i loved having him as a teacher so much that im taking medeival religious thought next semester just to have him again!

G Scott is the man - boring material, but he makes it relatable and fun to learn about. he is so smart, but not condescending. speakers he brings in are interesting - you dont need to read, just follow along in the book during class - paper topics are easy, but long

Do not take this class!!!  It is extremely difficult, does not deal with interesting subject matter, and is tedious.  I've never been so frustrated about a class or a professor, especially considering that it was an elective.

Dr. Davis humbled me with his superintellect. After having broken me down 3/4 into the semester, I stopped going to class for a month. Didn't matter. This man is so intellectually superior that he gives everyone at least a B, probably out of pity.

Dr. Davis is a true ivy league man.  He's taught at Princeton, Columbia and Stanford and is very smart and dryly funny.  There is lots of reading which is discussed in class every day and there were only 2 papers which make up the entire semester grade.
